sections.title: The Basics
points: A joint is a place in the body where two or more bones meet.
Joints allow for movement, stretching, and bending of the body.
They are divided into two main classes: Movable (Synovial) and Immovable (Fixed).

sections.title: The Lubrication Team
points: Synovial Fluid: A slippery liquid that acts like machine oil/grease to reduce friction.
Synovial Membrane: The capsule that holds and secretes the synovial fluid.
Cartilage: A smooth, slippery tissue covering bone ends. It acts as a shock absorber.

sections.text: If a joint lacks synovial fluid, bones will rub together, causing friction, heat, and extreme pain. Always use the B-L-B and M-T-B rule!

cards.mnemonic: Ligaments are like rubber bands for your bones!
Tendons are like strong ropes that pull the bone!
